Definition: from G4801; co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian:--yokefellow.
BiblicalUsage: Paul asks his true yokefellow to help Euodia and Syntyche agree in the Lord. The word is the same yoke-word as the joining in marriage, now used for a fellow-worker pulling in the same harness. Whether Paul means a named companion or a faithful friend, the role is clear — someone who shares the load of the gospel — and the name Syzygus itself means yokefellow, so some read the verse as addressing him by name.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul's appeal shows how much he valued the unnamed helpers. I hold that the gospel moves forward on the shoulders of yokefellows, not only on apostles.
